items.title: Four-Dimensional SCFT and Protected Observable Data
items.design_state: Step 1 authored definition; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement: Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. The selected classical model is the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills model with spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and global gauge group $G=SU(2)$ rather than $SO(3)$. Its field data are one $SU(2)$ connection, six real adjoint scalars, and four adjoint Weyl fermions, with the coupling and action normalization fixed by the selected model data. The gauge coupling $g>0$ is dimensionless in four dimensions. The model's sixteen-supercharge invariance is adopted as part of that classical model; this definition does not add a proof of invariance, a quantum measure, or a continuum construction.

items.title: Conditional Dimension of the SU(2) Quadratic Chiral Primary
items.design_state: Step 1 authored example; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
items.statement: Use the selected N=4 SU(2) field data and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $Z$ be the complex scalar component of the first canonical adjoint chiral superfield; its engineering mass dimension is one and its selected N=1 $U(1)_R$ charge is $2/3$. Suppose a unitary quantum SCFT realization has a local operator algebra containing the nonzero scalar superconformal primary represented by the renormalized composite $\mathcal O=\operatorname{Tr}_2(Z^2)$, and suppose this state lies in the chiral branch. Then $\mathcal O$ has $R$ charge $4/3$ and scaling dimension exactly $2$. This is conditional shortening data for this specified operator state; it does not assert that the classical action constructs a continuum SCFT or that every scalar observable is protected.
